binomial_family.note: exact integer tails validated against closed forms and against the published identity P(X >= k) = I_p(k, n-k+1); no drafting output is referenced

clopper_pearson_family.note: the lower limit is defined by P(X >= x | limit) = alpha; the check re-evaluates that tail at the returned limit

enumeration_accuracy.note: enumeration accuracy only; it says nothing about whether the asymptotic decision rule attains its nominal level

paired_family.note: at a null difference of zero the constrained root collapses to (n12+n21)/(2n) and the statistic becomes McNemar's; that published special case is verified as an algebraic identity. The constrained maximum can sit on the edge of the feasible set, where the score equation is not stationary; those cases are counted and checked through the polynomial residual instead, and none of them is infeasible

drafting_table_comparison.note: agreement on the exact-binomial family is expected because both implementations evaluate the same closed-form law; it is not evidence that the design is correct, and it carries no weight for the paired family, where the two implementations answer different questions

rejection_rule.constrained_root: 2 n q^2 - [(n12 + n21) - d0 (2n - n12 + n21)] q - n21 d0 (1 - d0) = 0, positive root
rejection_rule.decision: intersection-union: equivalence is declared only if Z(-margin) > z_(1-alpha) and Z(+margin) < -z_(1-alpha); a non-significant difference is never equivalence
rejection_rule.estimand: delta = pi12 - pi21 on paired base-item indicators
rejection_rule.exactness_scope: the enumeration of the joint law of (n12, n21) is exact; the decision rule itself is asymptotic and is not conservative by construction

nuisance_optimisation.bracketing: coarse argmax with its two neighbours
nuisance_optimisation.coarse_grid_points_rule: max(64, 2n), so that the grid is finer than the 1/n scale on which the lattice region changes
nuisance_optimisation.domain: q = pi21 on the null boundary delta = +margin, with pi12 = q + margin; feasible domain q in [0, (1 - margin) / 2]
nuisance_optimisation.independent_validation: windowed and exhaustive lattice sums are compared, and the refined maximum is never allowed to fall below the coarse-grid maximum
nuisance_optimisation.on_nonconvergence: retain the coarse-grid maximum and flag it

rejection_rule.statistic: Tango (1998) constrained-score statistic Z(d0) = (n12 - n21 - n d0) / sqrt(n (2 q~ + d0 (1 - d0))) with q~ the constrained maximum-likelihood pi21
